subject: AI & Agents
title: Shakey the Robot
description: A short lesson to help you apply Shakey the Robot.

hook.text: In 1966, a wobbly robot at Stanford became the first machine to reason about its own actions.

buildup.text: Shakey combined vision, movement planning, and logical reasoning in one system.

discovery.text: It could navigate rooms, push boxes, and follow instructions like 'move the block to the table.'

twist.text: Shakey moved at two meters per hour. Each action required minutes of computation.

climax.text: But the algorithms it pioneered — A* search and STRIPS planning — are still used today.

punchline.text: Slow and shaky, but the ideas were rock solid.

quiz.question: What was Shakey the Robot known for?
options: First robot to reason about its own actions
First robot to pass the Turing Test

details.summary: Shakey, built at Stanford in the late 1960s, was the first robot to integrate perception, planning, and action. It could navigate rooms, avoid obstacles, and push objects to achieve goals.
details.whyItMatters: Shakey demonstrated that AI could operate in the physical world, not just on paper. It pioneered concepts in planning and navigation that modern robots still use today.
takeaways: Shakey was the first robot combining perception, planning, and action
It navigated rooms and manipulated objects autonomously
Its planning algorithms influenced decades of robotics research

faq.question: What made Shakey revolutionary?
faq.answer: Previous robots followed fixed programs. Shakey could perceive its environment through a camera, reason about how to achieve goals, create plans, and execute physical actions — all integrated into one system.

faq.question: How does Shakey's legacy influence modern robots?
faq.answer: Shakey introduced the A* search algorithm for pathfinding and STRIPS planning language, both still used in modern robotics and AI planning systems. It established the framework for autonomous robot behavior.
